text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central bank extends deadline for potential buyers of six distressed banks out of the 17 taken over by the central bank last year.
- Government insistence on Import Duty Requirement papers as part of moves to clean up customs procedures, has been blamed for the low volume of imports in the first half of 1996.
- Government may close more diplomatic missions abroad, sources say. Nigeria recently shut its embassy in Canada citing economic hardship.
- Central bank queries 12 banks for violating guidelines on interest rates.

- Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group may visit Nigeria in October and be allowed to meet some political detainees, after talks between government and a Commonwealth delegation to try and arrange the visit.
